item.title: Why Trump is suddenly threatening Iran's last untouched nuclear site
item.description: Trump threatens to strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility, but military experts disagree over whether bunker busters can reach its chambers.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump is threatening to strike Iran’s deeply buried Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility — a site the United States previously left untouched while bombing the country’s other major nuclear sites, raising new questions about what may have changed.

Estimated to lie beneath at least 100 meters of rock near Iran's damaged Natanz nuclear enrichment complex, Pickaxe was designed to replace an above-ground plant capable of assembling roughly 6,000 advanced centrifuges each year before it was destroyed in 2020.

Iran said the replacement would be larger, more modern and built "in the heart of the mountain." Analysts believe the tunnels could eventually hold a centrifuge assembly line, an enrichment plant or equipment used in certain nuclear weaponization activities.

I'VE STUDIED MILITARY STRATEGY. TRUMP NOW FACES IRAN'S OLDEST BATTLEFIELD TRICK

Yet the administration has not said whether it has confirmed that centrifuges were moved inside — or why a site left untouched during earlier attacks now warrants a strike. Military experts also disagree over whether airstrikes could destroy Pickaxe’s interior or merely seal its entrances temporarily.

The same depth that could protect Iran’s nuclear infrastructure may place Pickaxe’s main chambers beyond the reliable destructive reach of America’s most powerful conventional bunker-busting weapon. Bombing its exposed entrances could deny Iran access without destroying the facility or anything stored inside.

Trump said Tuesday that the United States would probably strike the area "pretty soon" and "very heavily."

TRUMP THREATENS 'MAJOR MILITARY PUNISHMENT' FOR IRAN OVER FUTURE HOUTHI ATTACKS

His warning came after The Wall Street Journal reported that Israeli intelligence believes Iran moved thousands of centrifuges into Pickaxe last fall. Trump said the transfer "may have" occurred but added that the United States did not have it "on record."

"Maybe this one they have right," Trump said. "But it’s okay. It doesn’t mean anything unless they have the material."

"We follow the material," he added.

TRUMP SEEKS $672M TO STOP IRANIAN NUKES AS NEGOTIATORS WEIGH FATE OF URANIUM STOCKPILE

By "the material," Trump was referring to Iran’s enriched uranium, including uranium gas that centrifuges can further enrich to weapons-grade levels.

Before the June 2025 attacks, the International Atomic Energy Agency had verified that Iran possessed 440.9 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%, enough, if further enriched, for approximately 10 nuclear weapons under the agency’s standard measurement.

Most of the stockpile was believed to have been held at Isfahan, with additional material at Natanz and Fordow. Inspectors have since been unable to verify its amount, condition or present location.

The Institute for Science and International Security assesses that the material remains trapped at those three sites and does not believe enriched uranium has entered Pickaxe.

The administration has not said whether the United States independently corroborated the reported Israeli assessment, whether centrifuges are being stored or installed inside Pickaxe or whether nuclear material has entered the facility.

Storing centrifuges would not make Pickaxe an operational enrichment plant. The machines would have to be installed in connected cascades, linked to electrical, ventilation and piping systems and fed uranium gas.

Satellite imagery shows continued construction but no indication that Pickaxe is operational, according to the Washington-based institute. Images from February showed Iran adding concrete, rock and reinforced structures over tunnel portals in an apparent effort to harden them against airstrikes.

Analysts also observed smaller closed-roof vehicles near the entrances that could indicate Iran was outfitting the interior. The imagery could not establish what the vehicles carried.

Spencer Faragasso, a senior research fellow at the Institute for Science and International Security, said earlier U.S. and Israeli attacks prioritized Iran’s operating enrichment program. Based on what was understood about Pickaxe at the time, he said, there was "nothing of priority" inside that warranted expending valuable deep-penetrating weapons.

"The facility is still under construction, and it’s unlikely that a centrifuge plant is operating inside there," Faragasso told Fox News Digital.

But Faragasso said centrifuges could have entered aboard covered trucks without being detected in commercial imagery, making the reported Israeli intelligence plausible but impossible for outside analysts to confirm.

The reported transfer could help explain Trump’s recent focus on Pickaxe, he said. The facility is also one of the last nuclear-related sites of its size that has not been struck.

Trump did not publicly name Pickaxe during the opening months of Operation Epic Fury. It entered his public rhetoric July 13, when conservative radio host Hugh Hewitt raised the facility during an interview.

Trump said American surveillance had detected no activity there but called Pickaxe a possible target for a "nice big fat shot right into the front door."

At the end of the interview, Hewitt urged Trump to "go get Pickaxe Mountain."

"We’re going to take out Pickaxe Mountain," Trump replied. "Tell the Iranians to be ready."

The White House could not be reached for comment for this story.

The administration has not explained whether the recent threats reflect new intelligence, an effort to deter Iran from activating the facility or a shift from destroying existing enrichment capacity to preventing Iran from rebuilding.

Whether the United States could destroy Pickaxe from the air remains disputed.

Nicole Grajewski, an assistant professor at Sciences Po and nonresident scholar in the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace’s Nuclear Policy Program, said it would be "very close to impossible" to destroy the facility through an air campaign like the one the United States carried out against Fordow.

Pickaxe is deeper and more heavily fortified, she said, and does not have a publicly confirmed structural weakness comparable to those exploited there.

Retired Air Force Brig. Gen. Robert Spalding, a former B-2 operations commander, said planners would first determine whether the mission required destroying Pickaxe’s interior or merely preventing Iran from using it.

"You assess what the goals are, and then you assess the costs associated with making something not fit for use — or destruction," Spalding said.

If destroying the facility proved infeasible, he said, the U.S. could instead deny access and prevent Iran from bringing in the personnel and equipment needed to operate it.

The institute has identified two possible ventilation-shaft locations through satellite imagery, including one it considers probable. Without internal schematics, however, analysts cannot confirm their purpose or connection to the main chambers.

Faragasso said the shafts could provide weak points for deep-penetrating weapons, although the results of an attack might remain unclear.

"The facility is not invulnerable," he said. "There are options."

"At the minimum, the tunnel entrances can be collapsed," Faragasso added, saying a strike could also send damaging shock waves into the facility.

Grajewski said collapsing the portals would prevent Iran from moving personnel or equipment in or out without first undertaking an excavation visible to American and Israeli surveillance. Any effort to reopen Pickaxe could trigger another strike.

But Iran has previously excavated entrances to missile tunnels after they were attacked, meaning keeping Pickaxe closed could require continued surveillance and repeated military action.

Grajewski said a strike could provide the U.S. with a "symbolic win" against one of Iran’s most prominent remaining nuclear-related facilities but would not eliminate the broader program.

"It is a very high-value facility," she said. "But it’s not the entirety of the Iranian nuclear program."

item.title: 'Shame on you': Sherrill knew voter-roll bombshell was coming when she called Trump a liar, DOJ official says
item.description: Harmeet Dhillon says Gov. Mikie Sherrill knew about New Jersey's voter roll bombshell before she accused Trump of lying about noncitizen voting.
item.content:encoded:
The Justice Department's top Civil Rights official accused New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill of criticizing President Donald Trump's election integrity claims even though she already knew her administration was about to disclose a major voter registration problem.

In his July 16 address, Trump accused China of acquiring sensitive voter data and said U.S. intelligence agencies hid that revelation from the public while also alleging several Democrat-run states, including New Jersey, have large numbers of noncitizens registered to vote.

Department of Homeland Security data released in concert with the speech found more than 35,000 potential noncitizens are on the Garden State’s rolls.

"When the president came out with his Primetime speech last Thursday, I believe in the sequencing of events that has been laid out, she already knew that this revelation was forthcoming," Assistant Attorney General Harmeet Dhillon said.

'SHADOW GOVERNMENT': TRUMP CLAIMS INTEL COMMUNITY BRAGGED ABOUT HIDING CHINESE MEDDLING

"She knew it, and she still went online and called the president a liar and said he was exaggerating – Shame on you, governor."

Dhillon said governors willing to cooperate with the DOJ would receive assistance but warned states refusing to do so could face lawsuits.

"It's a bipartisan problem, actually. And I'm really looking forward to helping everyone who will work with us fix this problem. And if they won't work with, we'll sue them and we'll still fix the problem."

Following Trump’s address, Sherrill signed on to a statement with 23 other Democratic governors attempting to throw cold water on the president's wide-ranging claims, calling him a liar, as Dhillon said.

"It's deeply alarming that President Trump continues to try to undermine free and fair elections. No amount of lies and conspiracy theories can change the fact that our country's elections have repeatedly been proven to be safe and secure," read the rebuke, formally led by Kentucky Gov. Andrew Beshear.

TONY DOKOUPIL CLASHES WITH MARK WARNER AFTER THE SENATOR RIPPED CBS FOR AIRING TRUMP SPEECH ‘AS NEWS’

Sherrill’s co-signed statement went on to accuse Trump of trying to "intimidate and silence voters" while claiming Democrats are the ones "actually making life better for American families by lowering costs, creating jobs and protecting our freedoms."

"Ours is a winning message, which is why he is trying to undermine democracy."

Dhillon said Sherrill and all other governors should join with DOJ to investigate every substantive claim of election integrity violations, warning it is their own citizens who stand to be hurt.

"Every single person who voted illegally canceled out the vote of a New Jersey voter; that is shameful," she said.

"And instead of pointing fingers at the president, which is what Governor Sherrill did… she should be raising her hand to work with the federal government to clean this up ASAP because that's the vow she took when she ran for office and she got sworn in as the governor of her state is to protect her citizens, and her citizens have a right to vote."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Dhillon's letter gave Sherrill five business days, expiring Tuesday, to turn over voter data in the case. Meanwhile, Sherrill indicated to WCBS that she wouldn't be complying.

"It is not a surprise... the Trump administration wants to immediately weaponize this against people as opposed to focusing on making sure we're running free and fair elections," the Democrat said.

Asked about the accusation Sherrill knew about her own state’s motor-voter scandal when she accused Trump of being a liar, Sherrill spokesman Sean Higgins pointed Fox News Digital to comments she made after touring a grocery store in Essex County to sign unrelated legislation.

NEW JERSEY REMOVES 6,600 PEOPLE FROM VOTER ROLLS WHO WERE ELIGIBLE TO CAST A BALLOT FOR 2024 ELECTION

In response to a reporter's question on the scandal, Sherrill said her administration is moving quickly because Jerseyans deserve transparency.

"We're running an independent investigation right now to get to the bottom of exactly how this happened and what's going on, but it is not a surprise to me that the federal government that the Trump administration wants to immediately weaponize this against people as opposed to focusing on making sure that we're running free and fair elections," Sherrill said.

Pennsylvania, New York and several other states have also resisted DOJ requests for voter registration data, arguing federal law and state privacy protections limit what information can be shared.

The DOJ has also sued officials in some of the states over the election integrity crisis, including New Jersey Lt. Gov. Dale Caldwell.

item.title: Shark Week dangers hit home as man is badly bitten while saving pregnant fiancée from harm
item.description: Shark attack survivor Jacorey High says he fought off a 4-foot shark in Daytona Beach Shores while rushing his pregnant fiancée to safety. He is speaking out as he recovers.
item.content:encoded:
A Georgia man in his early 20s is recovering after experiencing a shark bite while protecting his pregnant fiancée at a Florida beach.

The man was wading in waist-deep water near the Dunlawton Beach Approach in Daytona Beach Shores shortly before 5:30 p.m. on Saturday — just hours before this year's Shark Week kicked off — when a shark estimated to be about 4 feet long bit his left foot and ankle, Volusia County Beach Safety officials told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"He was treated on scene by Beach Safety personnel and transported to a nearby hospital with non-life-threatening injuries," officials said.

SHARK SIGHTINGS SPIKE NEAR AMERICA'S BEACHES AS JULY 4 CROWDS HEAD TO SHORE FOR WEEKEND

The victim was identified by FOX 5 Atlanta as Jacorey High of Henry County, Georgia. High said his first priority was getting his pregnant fiancée safely out of the water.

"I realized right away it was a shark because of the way it bit down on my foot, but I was more worried about getting my fiancée out of the water," High told FOX 5 Atlanta.

High said the shark continued to pursue him as he tried to escape.

"Then it came up to try to get my arm. So I had to push it away from me. I ran, and it tried to get my other leg," he told the station.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

He described the shark as gray on top and about as tall as the distance from his waist to his feet, according to FOX 5 Atlanta.

After reaching the shore, High realized the severity of his injuries.

"I didn't really feel it until I got to the hospital, when they started giving me medicine for it," he said.

Doctors performed surgery on High's foot after the attack, and he told the station he expects his recovery could take about three months.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"Hoping that it didn't really mess up anything important in my foot so that I can go back to work," High said.

Fox News Digital previously reported that shark experts have urged beachgoers to stay alert this summer as sightings have increased along several U.S. coastlines.

Marine biologist Mike Heithaus of Florida International University told Fox News Digital that shark bites remain unusual, even during the busy summer beach season.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"People should always be aware of local conditions and listen to lifeguards, but shark bites are very rare," he emphasized.

He recommended that people avoid murky water, that they stay away from areas where large schools of fish are visible and that they avoid places where other people are actively fishing.

Fox News Digital reached out to High for further comment about what happened. 

Shark Week 2026 runs from July 26 to Aug. 1 on the Discovery Channel.

Forget about owning an NBA team in Las Vegas, just buy the UNLV basketball team.

No, you aren’t reading that wrong. A college hoops team has decided to lean into this era of NIL and revenue-sharing by putting its squad up for sale, at least according to UNLV head coach Josh Pastner and the athletic department.

In a world that is already filled with college boosters helping pay the steep salaries that come with transfer portal players or high school athletes, UNLV is just saying the quiet part out loud when it comes to purchasing an entire team.

Another crisis for Bill Belichick: UNC places GM Michael Lombardi on administrative leave amid investigation

For years, there have been Las Vegas entrepreneurs hoping to bring a team to Las Vegas, in hopes of joining the other professional leagues that have found a home in 'Sin City'.

But, Josh Pastner is hoping someone will bite on his proposition to ditch the NBA aspirations and put a fraction of that potential costs into college hoops.

CLOCK IS TICKING AS SENATORS TED CRUZ, MARIA CANTWELL PUSH FOR SEC, BIG TEN BUY-IN ON COLLEGE SPORTS BILL

"Buy the college basketball team. It’s legal now. You can be the owner of the UNLV Runnin’ Rebels men’s basketball team, and it’s a lot less expensive," Josh Pastner told Taylor Rocha. "You don’t have to spend over a billion dollars to own our team. I’m asking for $10 to $12 million to own our team, and you still get a great tax write-off. You can be as involved, and you can tell people you are the owner of the team."

No, he's not kidding, and I can't say I blame him for trying.

In fact, UNLV basketball put together graphics on what you could buy with $10 million, compared to owning your own college program.

Running out of time: SEC, Big Ten wait on 'Protect College Sports Act' revisions as August recess nears

"The UNLV Runnin' Rebels are one of the most iconic brands in college basketball. A program with a national championship, final four legacy, and a home in the fastest growing sports city in America," UNLV said in a graphic.

"With Las Vegas hosting NBA Summer League, the 2028 Final Four, and an NBA franchise on the horizon, the Rebels sit at the center of it all. And according to head coach Josh Pastner, for 10 to 12 million dollars, it can all be yours."

I mean, this might be enticing for someone.

Why not?

There are boosters across the country that are hitting the golf course or college tailgate with the main mission of letting anyone who will listen how much money they donated to the program in order to help purchase a player for the team.

I promise, it's happening somewhere as we speak. The only thing missing is a player/owner, like 'Jackie Moon' from the Flint Tropics. If you don't understand the reference, please take the time to look it up, I promise it's worth your time.

For college athletics, the return on investment is hard to justify for any donor. Besides their favorite team cutting down the nets, or hoisting a trophy at seasons end, there really is no true ROI for these boosters.

Sure, third party collectives have gotten creative in offering up a piece of the company to receive dividends on future income that is created by the athletes they invest in. But, being able to call up the university booster with large pockets that is looking to see their team succeed is also based off ego.

For UNLV, the school is offering a chance to own the team, and I still don't know exactly what that looks like if we're being honest.

Obviously, we're talking about courtside seats to the game, or sitting in the luxury box. But, I don't imagine a college basketball coach is wanting to take input on team strategy from someone who is writing the check.

I don't suspect Josh Pastner is going to really want the 'team owner' in the locker room at halftime complaining about the lack of offense from the shooting guards who were paid a large sum of money to produce points.

But, in terms of raising money to compete in the very expensive college basketball world, you have to start somewhere.

item.title: Global partners are joining the Trump administration and this FBI to take down scam empires for good
item.description: FBI Director Kash Patel details how Operation Sand Dollar, Operation Zephyr Exodus, and global law enforcement partners are dismantling scam centers.
item.content:encoded:
The FBI has launched a historic effort to eliminate global scam center fraud that steal Americans’ life savings and fuel some of the world’s most vicious criminal networks. These scam centers are industrial-scale compounds located in cross-border regions on the other side of the world that are run by transnational criminal syndicates that torture workers, steal and launder billions and target Americans and our allies alike. It is a massive, highly sophisticated web of criminality.

Thanks to President Donald Trump’s decisive leadership and prioritization of the battle against scam centers, this FBI has taken the lead in the fight — treating scam centers as a top priority threat to our public and a crucial part of our no-fail mission to crush violent crime and defend the homeland.

Fifteen months ago, we laid out a playbook to dismantle the problem. We went to the source and launched an initiative in Southeast Asia, working with partners in India, Thailand, Cambodia, Indonesia, and more to scuttle compounds and disrupt their communications capabilities. We joined our private sector technology and financial industry partners to trace infrastructure, seize malicious domains, follow the money, and hunt down the funding streams for their leadership. We launched sweeping ops like Operation Blackout to identify, locate, and annihilate the largest international scam compounds in the region.

In just over a year, this playbook has delivered historic results.

WHAT A SCAMMER SEES THE MOMENT THEY GOOGLE YOUR NAME

In April, working side-by-side with Dubai Police and China’s Ministry of Public Security, the FBI led Operation Sand Dollar — the largest scam center takedown in our history. We hit nine scam centers run by Asian organized crime actors, made 311 arrests, and seized thousands of devices that had been used to target Americans in the United Arab Emirates. Each of those centers was stealing roughly $6 million a year. Shutting them down meant saving victims $54 million in losses — just from a single operation. 

EXCLUSIVE: FBI ADDS ALLEGED COVID FRAUDSTER ACCUSED OF TAKING $5M FROM KIDS' MEAL PROGRAM TO MOST WANTED LIST

Or look at our work against the Prince Holding Group in Cambodia, a transnational criminal empire running guarded compounds that pumped out global scams. Our takedown, Operation Zephyr Exodus, led to an indictment of their CEO for wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy, and the forfeiture of roughly 127,000 Bitcoin — about $15 billion at the time and the largest forfeiture in U.S. history — ripping out the financial engine of a criminal syndicate that used its ill-gotten gains to attack everyday Americans.

In another operation, we went after the Tai Chang scam compound in Burma, operated by Chinese criminals. We seized domains and $30 million tied to this and other compounds. One more op — a joint effort between the FBI’s Bangkok office and our Thai partners — took down the Shunda compound, linked to hundreds of millions in losses. They’d used a Telegram channel with over 6,000 followers to recruit forced labor into a Cambodian law enforcement impersonation scam — and we seized it.

We are not just reacting after the damage is done. Through Operation Level Up, an FBI initiative supported by the U.S. Secret Service and other partners, we are proactively identifying potential victims in real time. So far, we have notified nearly 9,000 people, about three-quarters of whom did not know they were being scammed. We have prevented an estimated $562 million in losses and referred dozens of people for suicide intervention. That’s what it means to treat this as a no-fail mission.

FBI BOSS KASH PATEL DETAILS HOW AGENCY AND PARTNERS SECURED RECORD-SHATTERING FIFA WORLD CUP

The scale of our global offensive against scam centers is unprecedented. We’ve now opened more than 30 FBI cases, pursued or helped restrain assets valued at more than $15 billion, and helped drive hundreds of arrests. We’ve suspended more than 7,500 terminals, cutting off the internet lifeline that powers thousands of scam devices at a time — thanks to this FBI’s tremendous partnership with the private sector. And just this past week, we hosted the FBI’s first-ever Scam Center Summit in Thailand – bringing together partners from 18 countries and hundreds of law enforcement agencies, igniting our mission to ensure scam centers can never again take a foothold in the region.

Through these actions, we haven’t just protected Americans; we’ve freed thousands of trafficking victims from forced-labor compounds. And we’re just getting started.

None of this is possible if we work alone. defend the homeland from global scam centers, we rely on ironclad partnerships, with the Royal Thai Police, Dubai Police, China’s Ministry of Public Security, Cambodian National Police, Indonesian National Police, and India’s Central Bureau of Investigation, to name a few our allies across Southeast Asia. When we combine our world-class intelligence capabilities, overseas law enforcement access, sanctions, and cutting-edge technology, these criminals have nowhere to hide.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

What’s next? At our Scam Center Summit, I informed our partners we would be bulldozing these compounds to show the world what full mission success is and challenged them to be the first to participate in this historic effort. We will also continue to target every level of syndicate leadership to ensure total dismantlement of these organizations is achieved. Action is what matters, and it is what this FBI will continue to deliver thanks to the Trump administration.

This FBI will keep driving forward and dismantle compounds, seize billions, rescue trafficking victims, return people’s life savings, and rubble these networks. They may think they can target Americans from safe havens overseas. Perhaps they should read the above.

item.title: Savannah Guthrie delivers 'very specific' message to mom's kidnapper 25 weeks after her abduction
item.description: Savannah Guthrie posted an emotional Instagram plea with a "very specific" message directed at whoever kidnapped her mother, Nancy Guthrie.
item.content:encoded:
Savannah Guthrie delivered a "very specific" message to her mother's kidnapper on Monday, more than 25 weeks after the 84-year-old Nancy Guthrie vanished from her Arizona home.

In an emotional plea posted to her Instagram account, Savannah Guthrie appealed directly to whoever is responsible for the kidnapping, saying that her family is "in agony" and "will never stop looking for her."

"Do the right thing now," Guthrie urged her mother's unidentified kidnappers. "Make the right choice. Help us find her. Tell us where to look for her." 

NANCY GUTHRIE UPDATE: 25 WEEKS AFTER ABDUCTION, ELIZABETH SMART SAYS THERE'S ‘REASON TO HAVE HOPE’

"I'm coming on today with a very specific message. It has been months since our mom was taken from us. Our family is in agony. We are in a nightmare that will not end. Nothing about our situation has changed. We have done our part, and we will never stop looking for her. We will always ache for her and feel that hole in our hearts. The world can be a cruel and unforgiving place," Savannah Guthrie said. "I truly believe it is never too late to do right thing. Help us bring this situation to an end. For all of us. No matter where we've been and what we've done, I believe there is always a way home. Please make the right choice."

A federal source close to the Guthrie case told Fox News that Savannah Guthrie was in communication with law enforcement about releasing her newest video. It was her first message in weeks, as official updates have slowed to a trickle and there have been no signs of her mother's whereabouts.

NANCY GUTHRIE'S SUSPECTED ABDUCTION: TIMELINE OF EVENTS IN DISAPPEARANCE OF ‘TODAY’ HOST'S MOM

The family is asking anyone with information to dial 1-800-CALL-FBI and claim a reward of over $1 million. 

There is also a separate reward for information that leads to an arrest that can be obtained anonymously by calling 520-88-CRIME, Tucson's Crime Stoppers affiliate.

The elder Guthrie, 84, was taken from her home in Tucson's Catalina Foothills neighborhood in the early hours of Feb. 1, according to the Pima County Sheriff's Department.

The results of DNA testing and other forensics have not been made public as the case drags on without signs of Guthrie. A purported ransom note and an apparent follow-up message that claimed she had died have not been confirmed as authentic by investigators.

No suspects have been publicly identified.

Earlier in the case, two men were detained, questioned and released without charges after searches of their vehicles and family homes. Neither has been accused of wrongdoing in connection with Guthrie's disappearance.

Fox News' Matt Finn contributed to this report.

item.title: German officials want to know why Berlin attack suspect was free despite alleged ISIS support
item.description: German officials are left to scrutinize why the suspect in a violent attack in Germany was roaming the streets despite alleged ISIS sympathies.
item.content:encoded:
In the wake of the recent violent attack in Berlin near a pride festival, German officials are left to contend with the questions surrounding why suspect Abdul Ballout was free to perpetrate the assault despite his recent conviction related to supporting ISIS.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Monday wished to know how the violent assault could have been prevented.

"We must do everything to protect people in Germany as best possible from such criminals, from dangerous people who for whatever reason can’t be taken into custody," Merz said, according to The Associated Press.

German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt told public broadcaster ZDF during an interview that in light of the 21-year-old suspect's conviction and record of backing the Islamic State, it did not make sense that the man was roaming free.

"You can assume that it certainly would have made sense to put this person in custody," he noted, according to the report.

BERLIN PRIDE ATTACK SUSPECT KILLED IN POLICE CONFRONTATION: AP

Berlin Mayor Kai Wegner told regional broadcaster RBB in an interview that while he did not wish to question the independence of the court system, when it comes to the matter of this attack, "words fail me."

The suspect in the recent Berlin attack went to Lebanon last year with the goal of traveling to Syria to join ISIS, according to an English translation of a joint release from the Berlin Public Prosecutor's Office and the Berlin Court of Appeal, which noted that the man "was born and raised in Berlin and is a German citizen."

The attack on Saturday night left one dead and 29 injured, according to the AP, which reported that 21-year-old Abdul Ballout is suspected of plowing a van into people near a pride festival prior to apparently slashing people with a machete in what authorities think was a terror attack.

The suspect was killed by authorities on Sunday.

"According to current information, the 21-year-old allegedly attacked the special forces officers with a bladed weapon, whereupon they used their firearms," an English translation of a July 26 joint press release from the Berlin Police and public prosecutor's office noted. "The man suffered fatal injuries and died at the scene. The investigation is ongoing."

ISIS POISED TO EXPLOIT HISTORIC US IRAQ EXIT, TERROR GROUP 'ACTIVELY WAITING IN THE GAPS,' EXPERT WARNS

Earlier this year, a Berlin juvenile court convicted Ballout of preparing a serious act of violence endangering the state, and publishing propaganda supporting ISIS.

A news release from the Berlin Public Prosecutor's Office and Berlin Court of Appeal said the court sentenced Ballout to one year and 10 months in youth custody before prosecutors appealed.

Officials have stated that the man was granted a suspended sentence, but the news release states: "The decision regarding the suspension of this sentence on probation was deferred for six months pursuant to Section 57 in conjunction with Section 61 Paragraph 1 of the Juvenile Courts Act. The court also imposed various conditions on Abdul B., including placing him under the supervision of a probation officer. The court lifted the existing arrest warrant, as pretrial detention primarily serves to secure the criminal proceedings and does not constitute a prejudicial punishment."

FBI ARRESTS 3 MEN WHO ALLEGEDLY PLEDGED ALLEGIANCE TO ISIS, FUNDED DRONE ATTACKS TARGETING US TROOPS OVERSEAS

The news release noted that the case was not over, given that the appeals process had yet to play out.

"This conviction is not yet legally binding, as the Berlin Public Prosecutor's Office has filed an appeal. The Public Prosecutor's Office had requested a longer, non-probationary sentence for a juvenile and the continuation of the arrest warrant," the release noted.
